life_summary: Matthias Foss Cowley was born on August 25, 1858, in Salt Lake City, Utah Territory, and spent his formative years in the heart of the Mormon community. He came of age during the Church's most challenging period, as federal prosecution of polygamy intensified. Cowley became known as a devoted family man and prolific writer on Church doctrine and history. His marriage to Abbie Hyde produced LDS apostle Matthew Cowley, who became a prominent twentieth-century Church leader. His second marriage to Luella Parkinson produced Samuel P. Cowley, who served as an FBI agent before being killed in 1934. Cowley maintained an active intellectual life, publishing five major works on Church doctrine and history between 1902 and 1963.
church_summary: Matthias F. Cowley was ordained an apostle on October 7, 1897, by Wilford Woodruff, replacing Moses Thatcher in the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. He served in this position until October 28, 1905, when he resigned at the request of Joseph F. Smith, partly due to his involvement in performing marriages that contravened the Church's 1890 Manifesto against plural marriage. His priesthood was suspended on May 11, 1911, but was restored on April 3, 1936. However, he was never restored to his former position in the Quorum. The town of Cowley, Wyoming was named in his honor. He died on June 16, 1940, in Salt Lake City, from uremia resulting from kidney failure.
